A governed-deleted generation is closed. At the fact level (`dispute` of a tombstoned fact by its uuid, a governed pruning of one of its versions, the adapter's delete of a member of a deleted lineage) the answer is `already_deleted`; at the facade's logical-reference level (`forget`, permanent `forget`, `correct`, `dispute` by `target_reference`) the former owner reads the bare `fact_not_found` result, because the reference has no visible head. Either answer is the same whether or not another scope has since re-created the id, and neither moves or reads the live generation [...] The one further governed act is the escalation of a reversible pruning to a permanent deletion by a writer eligible for that generation: it keeps the tombstone's `deleted_at`, recorded version and lineage, erases the content, and neither reads nor moves a live generation another scope holds.

Versions are generation-relative ... After a governed deletion of the head the id reports `0` to any writer, a re-creation's receipt reads `v0 -> v1`, and the former generation's count never reaches the new one; the owner of the deleted generation still reads the version its deletion recorded (`tombstoned`, DUR-DEL-001).

W1.statement: A promotion from another project onto a live head is refused with target_unavailable, reports v0/v0 and a v0 snapshot, and leaves head, version, recall and history of the owner byte-identical.

W2.statement: correct, forget, permanent forget and dispute from another project read byte-identically (ids and timestamps folded) to the same call on an id nobody wrote, and change nothing.

W3.statement: The refusal holds after every restart; the scope binding is durable.

W4.statement: An override leaving required isolation domains outside the bound domains is a malformed proposal (ValueError with one fixed message) for any target; an override declaring a superset of domains plus the owner's project cannot replace or correct the head while (documented) it may delete or dispute it as an eligible reader; and a complete re-declaration of the owner's scope commits as the owner would ONLY because `overrides` is privileged host input that the facade does not authenticate (docs/44 'Scope is privileged host input'): this is host re-declaration, never end-user isolation.

W5.statement: The owner's own remember, correct and dispute stay admitted (a disputed head is recorded as disputed and, as documented, withheld from the owner's own admission while staying a visible candidate), and the same text in an unrelated memory of another project is independent.

W6.statement: A proposal refused for its target, and one parked by policy review, persist no episode, live and after restart; a committed proposal keeps its episode.

W7.statement: A refused remember, correct, forget or dispute attempt by another project, and a former owner's attempts on a re-created id, leave no event and no identifier or text in the live generation's public history payload; the refused project's history of the memory stays blank; the former owner's answers are the same with and without a re-creation.

W8.statement: A governed-deleted id reports 0 to any writer: a re-created generation starts its own counter (snapshot v0, before v0, after v1, history 1), a refused or policy-parked proposal on the tombstoned id reports v0/v0, and the former owner's view keeps the version its deletion recorded and cannot write, dispute or re-delete the id while the new generation is live.
